rationale: Record a source-derived refinement of the removed-leader bound and the state of the draft harness, so a later turn does not mistake either for a measurement. The reader cannot be changed under time pressure: the draft harness for this question was damaged by a bad copy while adding the PreVote scenario (duplicate declarations), so it must be rebuilt from the retained basis before any execution, and no execution is requested now.

investigations.discriminator: Whether PreVote alone (without CheckQuorum) bounds the removed leader's window the way the source predicts, and whether the forwarded route yields a stale answer in any configuration; both require a rebuilt harness before they can be measured.

interpretations.rationale: The measured account is unchanged and rests on receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45: the removed leader answers the read immediately with an index below the entry the actual leader had already committed (parsed index 14), the actual leader's own answer covers its commit index (index 4 in the same receipt's numbering), and the exposure ends when the removed leader steps down one heartbeat interval after the new leader is elected (indices 15 and 16), because the current leader answers the old-term heartbeat with its higher term. What this update adds is a source-derived refinement of that bound plus the state of the draft harness. The refinement: the code path that produces the step-down is the branch that reacts to a message from a lower term by answering with the receiver's term, and its guard is `(r.checkQuorum || r.preVote) && (MsgHeartbeat || MsgApp)` (raft.go:1133-1156); CheckQuorum is therefore not the only option that bounds the window - PreVote alone should make the current leader answer the removed leader's old-term heartbeat with its term and end the exposure after the same single heartbeat interval. That prediction is source-derived, not measured: the draft harness for this question was damaged while I was adding a PreVote scenario (a copied test body left duplicate declarations, so the file no longer compiles), and rebuilding it from the retained basis is the prerequisite for measuring the refinement. No execution is requested, and nothing about the PreVote case is claimed beyond the source reading.
counterevidence: The measured witness and its bounds are unchanged (receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45, parsed indices 12-16), including the control that the actual leader answers correctly and the measured step-down after one heartbeat.

The PreVote refinement is only a source reading: the same guard also fires when CheckQuorum is enabled, and the exercised configuration had both options off, so the reading does not replace the measurement.
The draft harness's current bytes are not a usable basis: duplicate declarations were introduced while adding the PreVote scenario, so any execution from it would fail to build.
limitations: The draft harness for this question must be rebuilt from the retained basis (fixed experiment bbdf8837c719466ba9f5044f34c9c29f-experiment or its predecessors) before the PreVote or forwarded-route questions can be measured; the damaged draft is not an artifact of the target.

The scenario requires the application to apply a committed change that removes the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; applications that set that option, or that stop the removed node, do not reach it.

The witness is at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipt shows the returned index is below an already-committed entry and that no confirmation message was sent. No state machine was run, so the miss of that write in a served value is a consequence of the contract, not something the receipt measures.
Other tick ratios, the PreVote-only configuration and the forwarded route remain unmeasured.

knowledge.assertion: IsSingleton is a size-only test over the configuration and never compares the single voter with the local node.
StepLeader answers MsgReadIndex locally whenever IsSingleton holds, using its own commit index and without a round.
A removed leader keeps leading by default while its proposals are refused and its read answers are not.
Lease-based reads force CheckQuorum, and the lease makes voters refuse higher-term vote requests while they still hear the leader.
